text:
This looks like early 2015. Unemployment is 5.8%, which fits roughly October or November 2014 (it was 5.8% in both months). The dollar is up 9.35% year over year, which fits late 2014. Headline CPI is 1.28% year over year, consistent with the November 2014 reading of 1.3% (October was 1.7%). The 10-year yield is 2.20%, which matches the end of November 2014 (about 2.17%).

Other cues also point to November 2014. The fed funds rate is 0.13%. Developed ex-US equity is down 3.9% over the month and 11% from its 12-month high, and gold is down 2.6% over the month. The 20y+ Treasury return of +3.9% over the month is a bit high for November, but October 2014 saw a big rally. The 3-month payroll average of 278k fits November 2014, when payrolls were reported at 321k, after 243k in October and 271k in September.

Headline CPI of 1.28% is closer to the December 2014 reading of 0.8%. That does not match, and November CPI at 1.3% fits better. I will go with November 2014.
